_comment: Hand-transcribed from the sources named in each citation. Values are quoted, not inferred; verify against the cited section before changing one.

rules.name: Normal academic load
rules.text: Normal academic load is fifty credits per semester.

rules.name: Registrable range in a regular semester
rules.text: UG students may register for up to 30 percent less or more than the normal load, that is 35-65 credits, subject to DUGC approval of the registration form.

rules.name: Maximum credits in a regular semester
rules.text: Maximum credits (including Credits for External Activities) a student can register for in a regular semester is 65.

rules.name: Under-load minimum
rules.text: Students identified as academically deficient may register for a minimum of 27 credits. Students in their final semester or on an extended degree may register below the minimum where only that many credits remain.

rules.name: Credit limits when registering project credits
rules.text: For students registering for Project credits (with or without course), the credit limits will be 35 to 65.

rules.name: Summer-term maximum
rules.text: UG students may register for a maximum of 27 credits in the summer-term. The summer-term is not a regular semester.

rules.name: Summer-term maximum when graduating
rules.text: Students expecting to complete requirements for graduation by the summer-term may register for a maximum of 29 credits.

rules.name: Credits for External Activities per regular semester
rules.text: A student may register up to 27 CEA credits in a regular semester and up to 9 credits in summer term; over the entire programme only 27 credits are allowed.

rules.name: Institute Core minimum for graduation
rules.text: Institute Core (IC): a minimum of 60 credits acquired, subject to the batch-specific course conditions stated in the manual.

rules.name: CPI required for an Honours programme
rules.text: Departments state a CPI criterion of 8.0 for the BTH (Honours) variant of their B.Tech programme.

rules.name: Maximum duration, 4-year programmes
rules.text: BT/BS/BTM/BSM/BTH/BSH: normal duration 8 semesters, minimum 7, maximum 12 for Y22 and later and for Y21 and earlier alike.
rules.citation: UG Manual 3.2, Minimum and Maximum Duration

rules.name: Minimum duration, 4-year programmes
rules.text: BT/BS/BTM/BSM/BTH/BSH may not normally be completed in fewer than 7 semesters, though graduation may be claimed before the minimum residency.

rules.name: Maximum duration, Dual Degree
rules.text: Dual Degree: normal duration 10 semesters, minimum 9, maximum 15.

rules.name: Maximum duration, Double Major (Y22 and later)
rules.text: Double Major: normal duration 10 semesters, minimum 9, maximum 15 for Y22 and later.

rules.name: Maximum duration, Double Major (Y21 and earlier)
rules.text: Double Major: maximum 12 semesters for Y21 and earlier, three fewer than for later batches.

rules.name: Credits a Minor entails
rules.text: A Minor entails the completion of 27-44 credits through specified courses within a discipline or programme.

rules.name: Slots a Minor course may occupy
rules.text: A student may take Minor courses in an OE, DE, ESO or SCHEME slot, as advised by the parent department's DUGC Convener. Minor courses therefore consume existing elective capacity rather than adding credits on top of the template.

rules.name: No CPI criterion for a Minor
rules.text: There is no CPI criterion to apply for Minors. Allotment of Minor(s) is based only on the availability of seats.

rules.name: A Minor may not be in the student's own department
rules.text: All UG students can apply for Minor(s) in any department except their own. Double Major students are additionally excluded from the department of their second major, and Dual Degree students from their PG department.

rules.name: More than one Minor is permitted
rules.text: A student may complete more than one Minor. Each student may apply for a maximum of three minors in each application cycle, at the end of the 4th, 5th and 6th semester.

rules.name: Seats available in a Minor
rules.text: Where the first course of a Minor is a compulsory departmental course, the department admits at least the smaller of 10 students or 20 percent of its batch strength. Where it is not, the department admits up to 20 percent of its batch strength. Allotment is by seat availability alone, so scheduling a Minor course never guarantees admission to the Minor.
